$comment: EXAMPLE ONLY. Every price below is a placeholder, not a quote.
Provider rate cards change; copy this file, then replace each figure with the
current published rate for the model you are actually calling. Roundhouse
reports savings against these numbers, so a stale rate card does not produce a
slightly wrong dashboard -- it produces a confidently wrong one.
Point ROUNDHOUSE_CATALOG at your copy.
"providers" says where each model's `provider` actually is: a base URL, the
path each dialect is served at, the environment variable its key arrives in,
and any static headers the gateway asks for. A model whose `provider` names
no entry here is refused at load -- with one exception, "openai", which this
build defines implicitly at the endpoint ROUNDHOUSE_OPENAI_API_BASE names, so
a catalog written before providers existed still loads unchanged. The key
itself is never in this file: `auth.env` names the variable, and the
credential a turn actually authenticates with is resolved per turn from the
control plane's three tiers (deployment, project, member).
"openrouter" below is a real, dispatchable definition: point OPENROUTER_API_KEY
at a real key and the three entries under it below are live. "dynamo-fleet" and
"anthropic" are not -- they are templates for the shape a self-hosted Dynamo
deployment or switchyard-server (base_url is your own frontend, serving
chat_completions) and an Anthropic account (serving messages) would use. Neither
dialect has a client in today's build, whose only transport is the OpenAI
Responses wire, and nothing in "models" names either provider, so both validate
without needing one. That absence is deliberate and this file is the reason:
a "models" entry speaking a dialect this build cannot serialize stops the boot
-- by design, since the alternative is failing one tenant's turn for a line in a
file -- and it stops it the moment ROUNDHOUSE_FRONTIER_UPSTREAM names a real
upstream, which is exactly what the README tells an operator to do next. An
example that cannot boot the binary it ships with teaches the format wrong.
Copy either definition, replace the placeholders, and add entries that name it
once your build carries a client for that dialect.
The three entries under "openrouter" spell out full, dated model ids rather
than a placeholder, because that is the point they demonstrate: an id with no
date suffix is not a rolling pointer to "whatever is newest" the way
"~deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-latest" is -- deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 is
itself a frozen snapshot dated 2026-07-31, and the *bare* deepseek ids (no
-NNNN suffix at all, e.g. deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash) are frozen too, pinned to
an earlier snapshot rather than tracking forward. Write the full dated id you
mean; "the latest DeepSeek" is ambiguous and this catalog has no mechanism to
re-resolve it later -- which is why a "~"-prefixed id under "openrouter" is now
refused at load rather than only discouraged here: the rule was worth stating,
so it was worth enforcing where the ambiguity is still cheap to remove.
openai/gpt-5.6-sol shows the same model reachable through
two different `provider` entries -- directly as "openai", or, as written
here, through "openrouter" -- which the catalog treats as two independent
prices and two independent (provider, model) identities, never one deduplicated
against the other.

correlaries.note: Replace this note with why. It is shown verbatim on the dashboard, because a reader deciding whether to trust the savings figure is really deciding whether to trust this sentence.
